title: 5 parallel coding agents testing SwiftUI: 11 GB → 150 MB RAM, 22 s → 2 s per check. No iOS Simulator (open source)
summary: Low-Future-9387 describes running an iOS app’s Designed for iPad slice as a headless Mac host, with one host per worktree, hot-reloaded views, and compact accessibility checks. The reported speed and memory gains come from one app and one trial per scenario; an iOS team can calibrate representative fixtures against the Simulator and retain device checks for Dynamic Type, transitions, gestures, and the keyboard.
takeaway: Use deterministic SwiftUI fixtures and a host per worktree for quick checks, calibrate render fidelity against the Simulator, and keep a real-device pass for interactions the Mac host cannot exercise.
